isting `/workspace/mcp.json` contains the URL but no credential. Unauthenticated direct initialization returns 401 `invalid_token`
; public OAuth metadata endpoints return 404. Supplying the provided `MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` as the CLI bearer token recovers connectiv
ity. An interactive OAuth flow is unnecessary with this supplied credential.\n\nThe configured account API supports catalog, tools
listing and the saved eval run, but several documented diagnostics, direct tool-call, trace, gate, model-catalog and persisted co
nformance routes return 404 with “Synthetic fixture does not implement this route.” The local MCPJam CLI provides the direct valid
ation fallback. These responses are retained in `requests.jsonl`; they do not establish that the MCP server failed.\n\n## Reproduc

e

With `MCP_SERVER_TOKEN` available in the environment, run:

```bash
/workspace/validation/validate.sh
```

This reads t
he existing server URL from `/workspace/mcp.json`, applies the credential at runtime, runs the pinned MCPJam CLI, and saves doctor
, conformance, and arithmetic evidence. It requires Node/npm, Python 3, and package registry access. No credential is embedded in
the scripts or reports.\n\n`api.py` reproduces public account API requests using `MCPJAM_API_URL` and `MCPJAM_API_KEY`. `requests.
jsonl` records responses, including the original run launch body shape through its saved result; rerun a cloud suite explicitly wi
th `serverIds: [\"server_fixture\"]`, since the suite has no saved server selection. Run creation used idempotency key `arithmetic
-validation-20261115-1`.\n\nNo account-owner or human action is required for these checks. No production billing contact or purcha
se was made.\n\nPublic references: https://docs.mcpjam.com/reference/public-api and https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/server-inspection
and https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/tools-resources-prompts. Saved documentation and OpenAPI snapshots accompany the evidence.\nMD\npy
